topic.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Knowledge Access
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a language model with an external collection of information. The retriever selects evidence that the generator can use, making knowledge access a separate component from what is stored in model parameters. This cluster studies retrieval chains, routing, technical-document evaluation, large data lakes, and gaps in what retrievers can find.
topic.whyItMatters: External evidence can improve specificity and support updating knowledge, but generation remains limited by retrieval quality. Relevant entities may be poorly positioned in an embedding space, leaving blind spots even when the required information exists in the collection.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives concern information retrieval and query learning. Later work combines dense retrieval with sequence generation. Recent studies emphasize realistic corpora, multi-system routing, temporal knowledge, and detecting or repairing retrieval failures before downstream answers are produced.
openQuestions: How can systems distinguish missing evidence from a failure to retrieve existing evidence?
What evaluations measure end-to-end faithfulness across changing, heterogeneous knowledge collections?
